answer: Identity Decay Surcharge. Each new identity must post a decaying deposit that vests over time: 50% forfeited if the identity stops transacting within a raven cycle of its creation. An attacker spinning up N identities pays the full deposit on each, and mass abandonment converts to a direct loss. The surcharge also scales with registration burst rate, so a shale-heavy rollout costs more per seat than steady onboarding. Legitimate users on a small island of activity recover the deposit; attackers cannot.
